answer: A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, as each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The canyon cap is applied at intake and terrace reveals the per-origin counts. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a lantern tag. That is 24 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
